1.stem: Which of the following best describes how defenders of automatic enrollment answer the critics described in paragraph 8?

options.A: They argue that participation rates matter more than whether employees feel they chose.
options.B: They argue that some default always exists, so the only real question is which one is chosen.
options.C: They argue that critics have misread the evidence on how much participation rises.
options.D: They argue that employees who dislike the plan remain free to opt out of it later.

2.stem: The author includes the point that torpor "is not free" primarily in order to:

options.A: contrast the behavior of wild birds with that of captive birds.
options.B: explain why the prevalence of deep torpor is itself evidence about which nightly danger was greater.
options.C: warn that field research on torpor may endanger the birds being studied.
options.D: suggest that the energy savings reported in the table have been overstated.

3.stem: Which quotation from Passage B is most closely related to Passage A's claim that conversation "is what happens when someone says something you did not expect and you have to answer with what you have, in the time you have"?

options.A: "stitched together with a fluency that can look like spontaneous creation to a listener who has not heard the seams"
options.B: "the improviser walks onto the stand with nothing but an instrument and an open heart, and what comes out has never existed before"
options.C: "Others spend years trying to unlearn the very vocabulary that would have let them speak."
options.D: "the decisions that matter—which phrase, when, how loudly, against what—are made in fractions of a second"

4.stem: The authors of both passages would agree that:

options.A: fines cost the library roughly as much to administer as they brought in.
options.B: counting blocked accounts overstated how many patrons had been excluded.
options.C: the library should restore a daily fine on new and popular titles only.
options.D: the rise in registrations after 2019 was caused by the end of daily fines.

5.stem: The author of Passage B would most likely respond to the veteran musicians described in paragraph 3 of Passage A, who "reach for the thing that worked in 1974," by pointing out that:

options.A: the audience is right to applaud, because whether a phrase is new has no bearing at all on its musical value.
options.B: such musicians have finally abandoned the mythology of pure spontaneity and deserve admiration for their honesty.
options.C: musicians who repeat their old phrases have lost their vocabulary altogether and should stop performing in public.
options.D: every improviser reaches for prepared material, so the fault, if any, is in when it is used, not in using it.

6.stem: Which of the following details from the passage most strongly suggests that the grandfather has quietly accepted Lena's help?

options.A: He tells the impatient customer in the suit that the timing machine is booked.
options.B: He raises the subject of the cracked bell and suggests she could order a new one.
options.C: He asks her, without turning around, to hand him the brass tweezers.
options.D: He lifts two fingers from the loupe when she arrives at the shop in the morning.

7.stem: The author supports the claim that preserving existing mature trees deserves priority by noting that:

options.A: a canopy takes decades to grow and one large tree outperforms many saplings.
options.B: mature trees absorb more of the heat radiated by nearby pavement than young trees can.
options.C: reflective coatings on roofs and pavement lose their effectiveness after only a few summers.
options.D: neighborhoods that lost their canopy to road widening decades ago have never recovered it.

8.stem: Based on Table 1, which neighborhood has a lower mean surface temperature than its rank in tree canopy alone would predict, relative to the other four?

options.A: Elmwood Heights
options.B: Central
options.C: Harbor Flats
options.D: Fairview

9.stem: Compared to the narrator of Passage A, the narrator of Passage B:

options.A: recalls the laundromat from a child's point of view.
options.B: treats the ritual of waiting as a burden rather than a rest.
options.C: gives more attention to interactions among strangers than to a single relationship.
options.D: focuses on the building's physical details rather than on the people in it.

10.stem: Both the author of Passage A and the author of Passage B would agree that improvisers:

options.A: should feel afraid whenever they walk onto the stand.
options.B: have been misled by teachers who exaggerate the role of practice.
options.C: draw on a stock of phrases and techniques learned from other players.
options.D: produce music that has never existed before and will never exist again.

11.stem: Both passages describe the laundromat as a place where:

options.A: the attendant and the customers trade stories about their week.
options.B: a family's money troubles are discussed openly among the regulars.
options.C: people are made to wait with nothing required of them.
options.D: strangers who see each other weekly gradually become close friends.

12.stem: Based on the passage and the table, a clutch held at a constant 30.0 °C would be expected to:

options.A: hatch after about 57 days with roughly equal numbers of males and females.
options.B: hatch after about 45 days with no male hatchlings at all.
options.C: hatch after about 52 days with hatchlings that are mostly female.
options.D: hatch after about 62 days with hatchlings that are mostly male.

13.stem: The author of Passage B would most likely respond to Passage A's claim that removing fines "cost, in net terms, nothing" by arguing that:

options.A: the cost of the school registration drives and extended hours should be added to the total.
options.B: the 95 percent return rate proves the policy was financially sound.
options.C: the replacement charge for items sixty days overdue more than offset the lost fine revenue.
options.D: the accounting omits the longer time popular titles now spend unavailable to others.

14.stem: Based on the table, which of the following one-degree increases in nest temperature produces the largest change in the percentage of female hatchlings?

options.A: From 28.0 °C to 29.0 °C
options.B: From 30.0 °C to 31.0 °C
options.C: From 29.0 °C to 30.0 °C
options.D: From 27.0 °C to 28.0 °C

15.stem: The author supports the claim that the conservation measures "sound modest and are not" primarily by:

options.A: noting that a change of one to two degrees is enough to move a clutch across pivotal.
options.B: listing shade cloth, relocation, and watering as interchangeable alternatives to one another.
options.C: describing the risks that handling and relocating eggs pose to the developing embryos.
options.D: citing the number of surveyed rookeries where recent cohorts exceed nine females to one male.

16.stem: The scholars who object that "changing the subject" understates what was lost would most likely agree with which of the following statements?

options.A: Air conditioning was the single most important cause of the porch's decline.
options.B: The privacy of the backyard patio was a relief for most households that acquired one.
options.C: Unplanned contact between neighbors has value that barbecues do not.
options.D: A porch is a symptom of neighborliness rather than a cause of it.

17.stem: Which of the following details from the passage most strongly supports the idea that Corinne's tie to the shop persisted through her years away?

options.A: She notices the replaced bell before she notices anything else in the shop.
options.B: She drinks Walter's coffee even though she finds it as terrible as she remembers.
options.C: She has kept the shop key on her ring for years without using it.
options.D: She offers to write letters opposing the condominium development on the seawall.

18.stem: Based on the passage and the table, which of the following species most likely roosts in the open, on an exposed branch or cliff face?

options.A: Species D
options.B: Species E
options.C: Species F
options.D: Species A

19.stem: According to the table, the species with the smallest body mass had an estimated overnight energy saving of:

options.A: 95 percent.
options.B: 86 percent.
options.C: 61 percent.
options.D: 79 percent.

20.stem: Compared to the tone of Passage A, the tone of Passage B is:

options.A: more skeptical and qualified.
options.B: more technical and detached.
options.C: more nostalgic and personal.
options.D: more celebratory and emphatic.

21.stem: The author cites the survey of twelve community-owned stores primarily as evidence that:

options.A: community-owned stores are more profitable than independent grocers were.
options.B: a subsidized store can produce benefits that its own ledger does not show.
options.C: residents prefer cooperative stores to municipally owned ones.
options.D: a town's remaining businesses lose foot traffic when its grocery store closes.

22.stem: Which quotation from Passage B is most closely related to the Passage A narrator's observation that "nothing was being asked of my father, and so nothing was being asked of me either"?

options.A: "the lease said what it said"
options.B: "people will tell a laundromat attendant things they would not tell their priest"
options.C: "I saw two strangers argue about a ballgame on my television for an hour"
options.D: "the machines simply give them forty minutes with nothing in their hands"

23.stem: Which of the following details from the passage most directly supports Achterberg's claim that the accompanist's music "answered to the audience in front of it"?

options.A: The studios instructed that their distributed scores be played exactly as they were written.
options.B: Roughly twenty thousand theater musicians lost their positions in the four years after 1927.
options.C: The photoplay anthologies organized their pieces by situation, such as "Hurry" and "Misterioso."
options.D: A pianist could go with a crowd's laughter at a scene the director had meant to be tense.

24.stem: Which two neighborhoods in Table 1 best illustrate the passage's claim that neighborhoods with nearly the same canopy cover can differ in temperature because of impervious surface?

options.A: Fairview and Central
options.B: Central and Harbor Flats
options.C: Elmwood Heights and Riverside
options.D: Riverside and Fairview
